title: Aggrega Wasm-plugin shared diagnostic
description: The single diagnostic shape every Wasm socket shares. A plugin reports one entry per issue it raises; the host surfaces it. The shape is a superset: every socket populates the subset it uses and omits the rest, so a diagnostic from any socket is one uniform structure. severity is an open string so each socket keeps its own vocabulary (a parser reports its own severities, an import reports error/warning/info, a publishing linter reports error/warning, a policy reports the build-outcome verdict deny/warn/audit); the host reads the severity value without the schema constraining it to one vocabulary.

Diagnostic.description: One issue a Wasm plugin raised: a severity, a human-readable message, an optional location, and optional socket-specific fields. Every socket that emits diagnostics emits this shape; each populates the subset it uses (a parser sets a location span, an import sets code and source_ref, a publishing linter sets rule_id and classification, a policy sets only severity and message, a renderer sets a structured location and suggest) and omits the rest.

severity.description: The diagnostic's severity, as an open string so each socket keeps its own vocabulary. A parser reports its own severities; an import reports error, warning, or info; a publishing linter reports error or warning; a policy reports the build-outcome verdict deny, warn, or audit. The host reads the value without the schema constraining it to one vocabulary.

code.description: An optional stable, machine-matchable code for the diagnostic, independent of the human-readable message. Absent when the emitting socket assigns no code.

rule_id.description: The identifier of the rule that produced the diagnostic, when the emitting socket is rule-based (a publishing linter). Absent otherwise.

classification.description: A semantic-version-impact classification the diagnostic carries, when the emitting rule assigns one (a schema-evolution rule). Absent for diagnostics that carry no classification.

source_ref.description: An opaque reference to the source element the diagnostic concerns (for example the identifier of a source node an import could not resolve). Absent when the diagnostic references no specific source element.

location.description: Where the diagnostic points, when the emitting socket can locate the issue. A parser fills the byte span; a renderer fills the structured position within a source document. Absent when the diagnostic has no location.

suggest.description: An optional remediation hint the emitting socket offers alongside the diagnostic. Absent when no hint is offered.

Location.description: Where a diagnostic points. It carries one unified locator that serves both a byte-precise position in raw source text (a parser fills the span) and a structured position within a source document (a renderer fills key_path, uri, line, and kind). Every field is optional; a socket populates the representation it can produce and omits the rest.

span.description: The span of raw source bytes the diagnostic locates, when the emitting socket parses source and can pin the issue to a byte range (a parser). Absent otherwise.

key_path.description: A dotted path to the offending element within a structured source document, when the emitting socket locates the issue structurally (a renderer). Absent otherwise.

uri.description: An identifier for the source artifact the diagnostic concerns, when the emitting socket knows it (a renderer). Absent otherwise.

line.description: A line number within the structured source document, distinct from the raw-byte line and column carried by span. Present when the emitting socket knows a document line (a renderer). Absent otherwise.

kind.description: An open string naming the source surface the location refers to, when the emitting socket distinguishes surfaces (a renderer). Absent otherwise.

Span.description: A span of the original source bytes: the byte offsets are the primary, exact location, and the line and column numbers accompany them for human-readable diagnostics.

start_offset.description: The byte offset of the span's first byte in the original source, zero-based.

end_offset.description: The byte offset one past the span's last byte in the original source, so end_offset minus start_offset is the span's length in bytes.

start_line.description: The line number of the span's start, one-based, for human-readable diagnostics.

start_column.description: The column number of the span's start, one-based, for human-readable diagnostics.

end_line.description: The line number of the span's end, one-based, for human-readable diagnostics.

end_column.description: The column number of the span's end, one-based, for human-readable diagnostics.
